answer: New identities enter through a narrow inlet: each account starts with a tiny throughput allowance and must complete publicly auditable tasks to climb a terrace of tiers, each tier demanding a larger verified-work deposit than the last. Only at the zenith tier can an agent vote or settle high-value deals, and the deposit is slashed if audits find faked work. Cloning an identity means paying the whole climb again, so a Sybil farm costs scale linearly per copy while rewards stay capped per tier.
